To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a simple strategy to improve the performance of grid connected voltage source converters is presented.

the proposed strategy can be used to compensate the distorted terminal currents caused by the time delays of the converter switches and that it does not require the knowledge of the converter's current controllers.

the proposed compensation technique is simple to be implemented in real time, it is able to compensate the dead time and turn on/turn off time delays of semiconductor switches, and it is able to ensure the operation in the linear modulation of the converter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the compensation of the dead time and turn on and turn-off time delays of a three phase voltage source converter in order to reduce the harmonic distortion of its terminal currents.
the compensation of the effects caused in the terminal voltages of the converter due to the time delays and semiconductor voltage drops of the switches.
the development of a simple dead time compensation methodology that can be easily applied in any grid connected voltage source converters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed compensation strategy is a simple, effective, and reliable method for grid connected voltage source converters.
the proposed strategy is simple and effective to compensate for the effects of dead time in the grid connected voltage source converters.

the proposed strategy is simple to implement in a digital signal processor and can significantly improve the quality of the grid currents, reducing the harmonic content and the total harmonic distortion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed strategy is simple, effective and robust to compensate the effects caused by the semiconductor time delays in the grid connected voltage source converters.

the compensation methodology presented in this paper is a robust and simple strategy for the compensation of the effects of the semiconductor switches time delays and voltage drop in grid connected voltage source converters.
the presented strategy can be easily applied to any converter operating in a wide range of power and frequency conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presented strategy is simple to implement, does not require any modification to the converter's pulse width modulation strategy, and is effective for all types of converters and grid conditions, including the presence of grid harmonics and voltage dips.

the compensation algorithm presented is very simple to implement in the controller of the converter and can be used in any grid connected converter, regardless of the converter topology, the number of phases, and the number of semiconductor switches per phase.
a simple compensation strategy can significantly reduce the current distortion and the DC voltage ripple in the converter.
